$comment: RPC-RETURN-CONTRACT-GUARD-1 — how every statically resolved .rpc() call is
allowed to handle its RESULT. A typed argument object proves nothing about
the value coming back: before this arc, 18 of 19 production callers asserted
their result with a handwritten `data as { ... }` that neither the compiler
nor the database ever checked, so a changed return shape compiled and ran.
approvedValidators — functions that genuinely validate an RPC result at
runtime. ONLY these count as validation; passing `data` to anything else
(notably `expect`) does not. Keep this list tiny and reviewed.
requireRuntimeValidation — functions whose result decides billing balances,
entitlements, authorization, ownership or destructive actions. For these a
compile-time type is NOT sufficient, and it usually cannot help at all:
every jsonb-returning function generates `Returns: Json`, which carries no
field information. Schemas live in core/database/rpcResultSchemas.ts.
exemptions — a call site that legitimately does none of the above. Each needs
a reason and the expected handling, and a stale entry fails the guard.
A call that never binds `data` is classified `ignored` and needs NO entry:
a caller cannot misuse a result it never took.
